field_insights.observation: Two database values in mas/yr: -3775.64 from Hipparcos and -3781.741 from Gaia DR3.
field_insights.interpretation: Both values represent the pmRA/pm_RA proper-motion component. They agree to ~0.16%, a small but expected offset caused by improved Gaia astrometry, different reference epochs, and known catalog systematic differences. Proxima's RA motion is strongly negative, corresponding to westward motion at ~3.78 arcsec/yr.
cause_hypotheses: Hipparcos vs Gaia reference-frame offsets
Proper-motion epoch propagation
Possible perspective acceleration at 1.3 pc distance

field_insights.observation: Two database values in mas/yr: 768.16 from Hipparcos and 769.465 from Gaia DR3.
field_insights.interpretation: Both values are the pmDE proper-motion component and indicate northward motion at ~0.77 arcsec/yr. The 1.3 mas/yr difference is ~0.17% and is consistent with known catalog version differences and measurement improvements. Gaia DR3 is the recommended value.
cause_hypotheses: Systematic differences between Hipparcos and Gaia
Different reference epochs
Small unmodeled acceleration in this very nearby star

field_insights.observation: Four database parallax values in mas: 772.3300170898438, 768.0665, 768.5, and 768.5004 from Gaia DR2/DR3, Hipparcos, and TIC.
field_insights.interpretation: These correspond to the Plx/parallax columns of the catalogs. The values agree to within ~4.3 mas, which is only ~0.6% relative error, and all imply a distance of 1.295-1.302 pc. The 772.33 mas outlier is likely a homogenized, photogeometric, or older catalog value; Gaia DR3's 768.0665 mas is the most precise astrometric determination.
cause_hypotheses: Different catalog versions and reduction methods
Photogeometric or statistical inference in TIC
Small systematic zero-point offsets between surveys

field_insights.observation: Two position-angle values: 282.4 degrees and 78.77 degrees.
field_insights.interpretation: The standard proper-motion position angle of Proxima is ~282 degrees east of north, corresponding to motion toward the northwest. The 78.77 degree value likely uses a different convention or is a complementary angle (e.g., measured from the opposite axis). The values are not physically contradictory once the position-angle convention is clarified.
cause_hypotheses: Different position-angle conventions in the two papers
One value quoted modulo 360 or 180 from a different zero-point
Possible transcription or formatting issue
field_insights.typical_range: Proper-motion PA convention: 0-360 degrees east of north; Proxima ~282 degrees.

cross_field_relationships.description: The two equatorial proper-motion components define the proper-motion vector. Total proper motion is μ = sqrt(μα*^2 + μδ^2) and position angle is θ = atan2(μα*, μδ) east of north. For Proxima, μα* ≈ -3781.7 mas/yr and μδ ≈ +769.5 mas/yr, giving μ ≈ 3859 mas/yr and PA ≈ 282°.

Parallax gives distance, d = 1000/π pc for π in mas. Proper motion and parallax together give the RA transverse velocity: V_α = 4.74 μα*/π km/s. There is no fixed one-to-one relation unless the space velocity is known; they jointly determine the tangential velocity.

Same measured quantity duplicated across catalogs; no physical relationship between a field and itself. Cross-catalog values should be consistent. For Proxima, Hipparcos gives -3775.64 mas/yr and Gaia DR3 gives -3781.741 mas/yr, agreeing to ~0.16%.

pm_total is the magnitude of the proper-motion vector: μ = sqrt(μα*^2 + μδ^2). Therefore pm_total ≥ |pmra|, with equality only if the DEC component is zero. For Proxima, μα*=-3781.7 and μδ=769.5 mas/yr give μ≈3859 mas/yr.

Proper-motion position angle is a trigonometric function of the components: θ = atan2(μα*, μδ), measured east of north. Thus pm_direction is computed from pmra and pmdec. For Proxima, pmra<0 and pmdec>0 give θ≈282°; a quoted value near 78.8° likely uses a complementary convention.

The DEC proper-motion component and parallax combine to give the northward transverse velocity: V_δ = 4.74 μδ/π km/s. No deterministic relation between μδ and π alone; the same μδ can occur at different distances if the space velocity differs.

Same measured quantity duplicated across catalogs; no physical relationship between a field and itself. Values should be mutually consistent. For Proxima, Hipparcos gives 768.16 mas/yr and Gaia DR3 gives 769.465 mas/yr, agreeing to ~0.17%.

pm_total is the magnitude of the proper-motion vector: μ = sqrt(μα*^2 + μδ^2). Therefore pm_total ≥ |pmdec|, with equality only if the RA component is zero. For Proxima, μ≈3859 mas/yr from μα*=-3781.7 and μδ=769.5 mas/yr.
Proper-motion position angle is derived from both components: θ = atan2(μα*, μδ) east of north. pmdec contributes the northward component; Proxima's positive μδ and negative μα* yield PA≈282°.

Same measured quantity duplicated across catalogs; no physical relationship between a field and itself. Values should be consistent within catalog systematics. For Proxima, values range from 768.0665 to 772.33 mas; Gaia DR3 768.0665 mas is the most precise, giving d ≈ 1.302 pc.

Total proper motion and parallax are related through the transverse space velocity: V_tan = 4.74 μ/π km/s, with μ in mas/yr and π in mas. There is no universal pm-parallax relation; for a fixed transverse velocity, μ is inversely proportional to distance.

Proper-motion direction is determined by the star's space-velocity components projected on the sky, not by its distance. Therefore parallax and pm_direction have no direct physical or statistical relationship. Proxima's pm_direction ≈ 282° while its parallax ≈ 768 mas, but these are independent astrometric parameters.

Both are polar-coordinate representations of the same proper-motion vector, but no physical law relates the total magnitude to the position angle alone. For a given pm_total, pm_direction can have any value; they are linked only through the components: pmra = μ sinθ, pmdec = μ cosθ.

suitable_use_cases: Cross-catalog astrometric validation for nearby high-proper-motion stars using Hipparcos, Gaia DR2/DR3, and TIC values
Demonstrating proper-motion vector composition and consistency checks between pmra, pmdec, pm_total, and pm_direction
Teaching and benchmarking unit-conversion pipelines for astrometric fields (mas/yr vs arcsec/yr)
Combining parallax and proper motion to estimate tangential velocities for Proxima Centauri, provided reference epochs and uncertainties are handled
Testing catalog cross-match and field-normalization workflows in an astrometric knowledge-base context
limitations: Several fields are duplicated across catalogs without explicit provenance or epoch metadata, so apparent discrepancies are expected and require careful sourcing
Proper-motion position angle has two inconsistent values (282.4 deg vs 78.77 deg) indicating different conventions or possible formatting issues that must be resolved before use
The conflict status 'Needs_Unit_Fix' and 20 normalization modifications reveal unit and format nonuniformity in the raw extraction
Coverage gaps exist: many sources lack pm_total, pm_direction, pm_source_flag, and some lack parallax or pm_ra/pm_dec, preventing complete per-source kinematic analysis
TIC parallax outlier (772.33 mas) and Hipparcos-Gaia offsets (~0.16% in pmra, ~0.17% in pmdec) reflect known catalog systematics rather than true physical variability
No uncertainties or reference epochs are provided in the records, limiting formal error propagation and rigorous astrometric fitting
recommended_caveats: Use Gaia DR3 astrometry as the primary reference for Proxima Centauri, and treat Hipparcos and TIC values as secondary or cross-checks
Convert all proper motions to the same units and component convention (e.g., mas/yr for mu_alpha* and mu_delta) before combining or comparing
Verify the position-angle convention explicitly; proper-motion PA is normally measured east of north from atan2(mu_alpha*, mu_delta)
Do not mix values from different epochs or catalogs without proper-motion and parallax propagation to a common epoch
Apply Gaia parallax zero-point corrections and quality cuts before deriving distances from parallax
Treat records missing pm_source_flag or uncertainties as lower confidence and exclude them from precision-critical analyses
Trace each value to its original catalog or paper and cite the exact source version when publishing results

overall_narrative: The analysis evaluates astrometric data for Proxima Centauri across 13 fields and 13 cross-field relationships, receiving a good overall grade. Proper-motion components agree to ~0.16–0.17% between catalogs, confirming expected offsets from Gaia improvements and epoch differences, with the declination component indicating northward motion. Parallax values agree within ~0.6% and consistently place the star at 1.295–1.302 pc, aside from one clear outlier (772.33 mas). The proper-motion position angle discrepancy (282° vs 78.77°) likely reflects differing conventions rather than physical differences. Overall, the dataset strongly supports the known astrometric solution for Proxima, with only minor catalog-specific variations.
